title: 2011 HMMT November Guts Problem 23
statement: Let \(N=\overline{5 A B 37 C 2}\), where \(A, B, C\) are digits between 0 and 9 , inclusive, and \(N\) is a 7 -digit positive integer. If \(N\) is divisible by 792 , determine all possible ordered triples \((A, B, C)\).

solutions.text:
\((0,5,5),(4,5,1),(6,4,9)\) First, note that \(792=2^{3} \times 3^{2} \times 11\). So we get that

\[\begin{gathered}
8|N \Rightarrow 8| \overline{7 C 2} \Rightarrow 8 \mid 10 C+6 \Rightarrow C=1,5,9 \\
9|N \Rightarrow 9| 5+A+B+3+7+C+2 \Rightarrow A+B+C=1,10,19 \\
11|N \Rightarrow 11| 5-A+B-3+7-C+2 \Rightarrow-A+B-C=-11,0
\end{gathered}\]

Adding the last two equations, and noting that they sum to \(2 B\), which must be even, we get that \(B=4,5\).
Checking values of \(C\) we get possible triplets of \((0,5,5),(4,5,1)\), and \((6,4,9)\).
